CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Advanced maternal age (43 years)
Gestation at Sampling: 16 weeks
Clinical Indication: Screening for Down syndrome and other chromosomal abnormalities
Previous Testing: Rapid PCR analysis performed

TEST PERFORMED
G-banded Chromosome Analysis

METHODOLOGY
Amniotic fluid cells were cultured according to standard protocols. Metaphase chromosomes were G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa staining. A minimum of 15 cells were analyzed at 550 band resolution. Two independent cultures were examined.

RESULT
Karyotype: 46,XY

Normal male karyotype

No evidence of trisomy 21 or other numerical abnormalities detected
No structural chromosomal abnormalities identified at this resolution

Cells Analyzed: 20 metaphases from 2 independent cultures
Band Resolution: 550 bands

INTERPRETATION
This analysis reveals a normal male chromosomal complement. There is no evidence of Down syndrome (trisomy 21) or other common autosomal trisomies (13, 18). No numerical or major structural chromosomal abnormalities were detected.

This result supersedes the previous rapid PCR analysis. The karyotype analysis provides comprehensive assessment of all chromosomes, whereas rapid PCR targets specific chromosomes only.

LIMITATIONS
This test cannot exclude all chromosomal abnormalities. Small deletions, duplications, or rearrangements below the resolution of conventional cytogenetics may not be detected. Low-level mosaicism (<10%) may not be identified. This test does not screen for single gene disorders.

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further cytogenetic testing indicated based on these results. Continue routine prenatal care.
